verses.1: As Lakshmana was comforting his affectionate brother, Vibheeshana came to Rama assigning the troops to reach their respective places.
verses.2: Accompanied by the four ministers surrounded by four ministers resembling leaders of elephants, who looked dark like collyrium, Vibheeshana came to highsouled Rama. He witnessed Vanaras whose eyes were filled with tears.
verses.3: He (Vibheeshana) saw the great soul, the delight of the Ikshvaku race deluded, distressed, and lying on the lap of Lakshmana.
verses.4: He (Vibheeshana) saw the great soul, the delight of the Ikshvaku race deluded, distressed, and lying on the lap of Lakshmana.
verses.5: Vibheeshana was pained to see Rama immersed in grief, depressed in spirit, and asked for What is all this grief for?
verses.6: Lakshmana looking at Sugriva's face and also at the Vanaras, his eyes bathed in tears spoke in a dull tone.
verses.7: "O Noble one! On hearing Hanuman that Sita is killed by Indrajith, Rama is deluded', said Lakshmana to Vibheeshana."
verses.8: Vibheeshana spoke these meaningful words to Rama, who was unconscious, restraining Saumithri from speaking.
verses.9: "I think that what has been spoken by Hanuman as truth (that Sita has been killed) is like drying up an ocean."
verses.10: "O mighty armed Rama! with reference to Sita, you do not know Ravana's opinion. He will never kill Sita."
verses.11: 'Though entreated by me again and again, wishing his welfare, saying “Release Vaidehi”, he never heeded my word.'
verses.12: 'Not by conciliation, nor by sowing dissension, nor by gifts — how then by war? She cannot even be seen by any means whatsoever.'
verses.13: 'That rakshasa has gone back after merely deluding the monkeys. Know, O mighty-armed one, that daughter of Janaka to have been a mere creation of illusion.'
verses.14: 'He will perform a sacrifice at the sanctuary called Nikumbhila; having offered the oblations and returned, even to the gods together with Indra—'
verses.15: '—that son of Ravana becomes unassailable in battle. Surely, seeking to bewilder, he has employed this illusion.'
verses.16: 'Wishing, dear one, to put an obstacle in the way of the monkeys' valour, he has done this. Let us therefore go there with the army before that rite is completed.'
verses.17: 'Cast off, O tiger among men, this false grief that has come upon you; for the whole army loses heart on seeing you wasted with sorrow.'
verses.18: 'Stay here with a tranquil heart, full of courage, and send Lakshmana with us, together with the forces that follow.'
verses.19: 'This tiger among men with his sharp arrows will make Ravana's son abandon that rite; then will he become fit to be slain.'
verses.20: 'These sharp and keen arrows of his, winged with feathers, fierce as birds of prey, shall drink his blood.'
verses.21: 'Therefore, O mighty-armed one, commission the auspicious-marked Lakshmana for the destruction of that rakshasa, as the wielder of the thunderbolt lets loose his bolt.'
verses.22: 'O best of men, delay is not proper in the slaying of the foe — what can be done today, do. Loose your arrow-power for the destruction of the enemy, as the great Indra did in crushing the city of the asuras.'
verses.23: 'For that bull among rakshasas, his rite complete, becomes invisible in battle even to the gods and asuras; and should he give battle with his rite accomplished, even the gods would stand in great peril.'
